_comment: DEPARTMENTAL POLICY, one file for the whole fleet.
The deploy script sets `group` per OU and every workstation picks the
matching overlay. One GPO, one artifact in change control.
WHAT A DEPARTMENT CANNOT CHANGE
Hard identifiers -- SSN, payment card, bank/routing number, driver
license, bulk record exports, credentials, private keys -- BLOCK in every
department, on every site, in every mode. No overlay below can soften
them, and exemptRules cannot reach them. See ALWAYS_ENFORCE in policy.js.
This is not a tuning choice. A disclosure is equally bad whichever
department causes it: the resident is harmed the same, and the county's
notification obligation is the same. There is also no job function that
requires pasting a live SSN into a public AI service, so a hard floor
costs nothing in false positives.
WHAT A DEPARTMENT CAN STILL CHANGE
Contextual rules -- dob, medical vocabulary, CJIS terms, internal_host,
gov_email, case_number. These are genuinely noisy in some job functions:
'patient' is a disclosure in Health and an ordinary noun in Facilities.
Forcing them fleet-wide produces the false positives that get a tool
uninstalled or worked around, which protects nobody.
So the split is: WHAT counts as a leak is fixed. HOW MUCH ambient noise a
department tolerates is tunable.
Overlay semantics: merged ON TOP of the baseline, so an overlay states
only its differences. Objects merge key-by-key; arrays replace wholesale.

_why: County Attorney. Privileged material, active litigation, sealed
records. Strict means warn-severity findings block too, and an
uninspectable attachment is refused rather than flagged -- for this
group 'we could not read the PDF' is not an acceptable outcome.
Personnel files, discipline, medical and benefits data. Same posture
as legal, except HR genuinely lives in Workday all day -- which is
already in neverScan, so nothing here needs to loosen for it.
CJIS applies. The cjis and cjis_id rules exist for this group above
all others, and the FBI CJIS Security Policy makes disclosure to a
third-party service a reportable event, not a policy preference.
Note media_ai is enforced here rather than warned: an investigator
uploading a suspect photo to an image tool is a real scenario and it
is not one to leave to a confirm dialog.
HIPAA covered functions. The medical rule is warn-severity by default
because the vocabulary is noisy in general office use -- but in this
department a prompt containing 'patient' and 'diagnosis' is exactly
what needs stopping, so strict promotes it to a block.
The one group with a legitimate daily need to paste text that trips
internal_host: stack traces, config files, subnet plans. Exempting that
ONE contextual rule is the difference between a tool they use and a tool
they route around.
The exemption CANNOT reach hard identifiers. An API key, an SSN, or a
card number in an IT prompt blocks exactly as it does in Legal's -- the
floor in policy.js is not exemptable. IT is the group most likely to
paste a live credential, so this matters here more than anywhere.
code_ai is warn rather than enforce so a snippet is not refused outright.
That softens contextual findings only; hard identifiers still block.
Parcel and address data is largely public record in Texas. case_number
fires constantly on parcel exports where it means a survey reference, not
a criminal cause.
Exempting it does NOT weaken PII handling: an SSN or DOB on a parcel
record still blocks, because those are floor rules.
Public information office. Their job is producing material intended for
release, and gov_email fires on every press contact they write.
warn mode applies to CONTEXTUAL findings only. An earlier version of this
file let warn mode plus the gov_email exemption downgrade a real SSN to a
dismissible warning -- 'jane@county.gov re: her SSN 123-45-6789' resolved
to WARN. That was a genuine hole and it is now closed: hard identifiers
block here exactly as they do in Legal.
Drafting a press release is lower risk than handling case files. Leaking
a resident's SSN is not, and the destination does not care who sent it.
Everyone not in a named group. Deliberately the baseline and nothing
more -- if a department needs an exception, give it a group so the
exception is visible in change control rather than quietly widening
the default for the whole county.
Rollout group. Monitor CONTEXTUAL findings so a department can be
measured before enforcement: read the morning report, count how many
warns would have been false positives, then promote.
monitor does NOT extend to hard identifiers. A pilot user who pastes an
SSN is still blocked -- 'we were still evaluating' is not a defence to a
disclosure, and a pilot that permits real leaks is not a pilot, it is an
unmonitored gap.
